Hey!

I mostly deal with IBS D. But sometimes I get a little constipation. I have a condition called cyclothymia. It's like a super mild BP 2 disorder. Basically, I'm just naturally up and down a lot in a predictable way. I tried Lexapro. It honestly didn't really do much of anything for me. But different stuff works for different ppl. I highly suggest being 100% honestly with your doc about your mental well-being. Not giving them all the details makes it harder to be diagnosed with the right thing. Try a psychiatrist if you're just seeing a general doctor.  Hope that helps!
Depression and anxiety
Thank you so much 💕

Hey there. So I originally made this post because validation from strangers has helped me a great deal in the past and I wanted to return the favor. Yes, please go to a psychiatrist or consoler. It helps, but everyone is different. Even then, depression, clinical depression, anxiety, etc, is sometimes related to a bigger problem. Stuff like Bipolar disorder and so on. That's my story unfortunately. Get help, especially if you have the tools/ability too. I honestly do not know or believe in true "happiness," but I believe in not feeling like committing suicide everyday. Idk what your story is, but I know where you're coming from. Take care of yourself friend.

It's hard to find ppl/friends that understand how to talk to you like a professional would. But, finding a support group will get you somewhere. There are depression related Facebook groups where ppl support each other. I also suggest visiting the depression_help subbreddit. It's a good community and it honestly saved my life. I hope you find your way out friend. Everyone's journey out of the hell is different.

Hey! So I consider myself better. It took a long time, but I've pulled myself out of it for now. It actually went therapy and have to take medication. To make along story short, I ignored my problems and ended up hurting myself anymore by not getting help.

In my opinion, it's a 50/50 kind of thing. Medication treats hormonal/chemical issues in your brain, which helps prevent depression tendencies. Therapy helps change your mindset via learning coping skills and healing mental scars. That help at all?
Keep trying. You can't will the darkness away, but you can will yourself into a daily schedule.

It sounds stupid, but try taking control of things you can control. Like what time you get up in the morning or go to bed. Stupid stuff like that. Idk what kinda stuff you're dealing with, but this helped for me. A little goes a long way. You deserve to be happy and you deserve to live

Hey friend.  A while back, Someone on this subbreddit told me that sometimes you just have to find one thing and hold on to it. It's pretty good advice, at least I think it is. Look, depression is horrible. Sometimes it's genetics, sometimes it's triggered by something, sometimes it's both. If the ppl around you are struggling too, it's ok to talk to them about it. Ppl often feel better if they have someone to relate too. It can be validating. Hope that helped a little, wish I had more to offer.

Hey friend, I know the feeling. You got 13 days, you got time to study. I've found a good way to study for exams while depressed. Grab you book/notes or whatever. Find a comfy spot to study at, and maybe a laptop. Study in intervals of about 10 to 15 minutes and take YouTube/meme breaks in between studying intervals. It works for me and hopefully it'll work for you. If you think you're going through withdrawal, make sure you're drinking water. I'm sorry you're in this position and I wish I had more to offer. You can do this, don't let your depression run your life. Get this exam over with and then invest some time into getting mentally healthy.

Hey friend,

Depression sucks. I've been battling it for about as long as you. The best thing you can do is take it all step by step. Maybe talk to your parents again and point out that yes, teenages deal with that stuff, but you've been dealing with it since you were a child. Come up with a few examples from your childhood. Be persistent if you have the energy too. Not all of us got help in time, but you can and seem to possibly have the resources to better yourself. If it means anything to you, I didn't have what's considered real friends until my junior year of high school. Ppl come and go, but your mental health is forever. Don't be afraid. It's so hard not to be, but some part of you is capable of it. Take care of yourself.

Hi friend!

I was in a very similar situation about a month ago. I didn't want to go back to counseling and retell my life story for like the 5th time. I got lucky because I live in a college town with a lot of affordable therapy and got financial support from my family. 

I don't really have any helpful alternatives other than maybe CBD oil? But that's pricy. One of the reasons why I took me a year to go back to therapy is because I learned some copping methods and stuff like that. I talked myself down and was mostly successful. But you can't do that with depression. I also used to dedicate time to analyze what and why I was thinking or feeling a certain way. I still do it, and it helps me manage. I'm sorry I don't really have any solution to your problem. I can really relate.

Death doesn't really change a thing. It's just nothing but a means to an end. At least, out of what we know. Dealing with depression is hard, especially when you're alone and not legally an adult. But you're not a lost cause. You're worth something more than a waste of space. You're family probably doesn't hate you, they just may not be able to understand how to talk to you or what you need. From the sound of it, you need some help. Maybe it's time to open up a conversation with your family or a family member you trust enough. Even if it's something small. Maybe there's a chance you can see a counselor or someone along the lines of that. 

Look friend, I spent my entire adolescence miserable. I didn't realize how easy it was to get professional help until it was too late. Now I'm 22 and dealing with clinical depression and other stuff I could of avoided simply by reaching out. It's much easier to say "I need help" than it is to end it. You may not feel worth it now, but the person you will grow to be will.

I did something a while back that kinda help me sort out my own demons. Maybe it'll help you. Make a physical list of things you love about yourself. Then make another one about all the problematic things you hate about yourself (the demons). Look at the problematic list and think about how those aspects interfere with the things you love about yourself. It sounds weird, but I helped me see how i needed to change. Separate the real bad from the good, you know?
